items.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022
items.q: I was playing along with a Count Basie record

ctx.x: And did you have a similar experience?

I did, several. The first one I would say would be when I heard one of — when I heard Dexter Gordon. Because he was so melodic and he was so swinging, and that’s what I responded to. And then the next time I still remember it, I was playing along with this, it was when I was a lead alto player and I was playing along with a Count Basie record and I don’t know, it think it was Willie Smith, the lead alto, he had a high B flat, just the one on top of the staff, and I finally got the alto sound I’d been trying to…
My one note, was Cannonball Adderley, when he played “Mercy, Mercy, Mercy” and he went [scats]. I went “Oh, I have to play like that, that one note.” Isn’t that amazing how that can just like —
